newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles County told to repay benefits - paper.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles County told to repay benefits - paper.

text.p: A California appeals court has ordered Los Angeles County to repay welfare benefits denied to tens of thousands of recipients from 1993 to 1995, according to a published report on Saturday.
The court of appeal ordered the county to pay retroactive benefits to general relief welfare recipients, whose grants were cut by $73 from 1993 to 1995, the Los Angeles Times reported.
The ruling could cost the county up to $160 million, attorneys involved in the case said.

In 1993, a class action lawsuit, dubbed the Gardner case, was filed by the Western Center on Law and Poverty and other public interest law firms on behalf of Los Angeles County general relief recipients. The lawsuit demanded that the county maintain the level of welfare benefits.
A state trial court refused to issue a preliminary injunction against the county. But the trial court decision was reversed by the court of appeal in 1995.
In 1996, attorneys for the welfare recipients asked the trial court to order the county to repay those recipients whose benefits were reduced in 1993, 1994 and 1995.
The trial court agreed, ordering the county to pay retroactive benefits to about 100,000 welfare recipients.

The county appealed the trial court decision back to the state court of appeal, which has now ordered county supervisors to repay the money with interest and to pay all the plaintiffs' legal fees and other costs, the Los Angeles Times reported.

Attorneys involved in the case said the county could be liable to pay up to $160 million. The amount the county would be forced to pay, however, would depend on the number of welfare recipients that file claims.
Los Angeles County is expected to appeal the decision to the state Supreme Court, the Los Angeles Times reported.
